answer: In an island market where AI agents trade saffron, each agent’s voting weight equals the tokens it locks for 30 days. Creating a spiral of fake accounts adds no influence: dividing 100 tokens among 1,000 identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To control one-third of the vote, an attacker must lock tokens worth half the honest agents’ combined stake, tying up capital that cannot be reused during the lock.
